title: Outcome Tethering: company-level OKR -> initiative ledger and decision runway
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket scopes and delivers a lightweight, company-level "Outcome Tether" ledger that maps top-level OKRs to active initiatives, owners, quantitative success signals, gating criteria, and decision runways for re-prioritization. The ledger is intended to be the single source-of-truth used by product, engineering, design, and GTM when making trade-offs across Dedicated / Hosted / Private product investments.

Why now:
- We frequently surface competing asks across platform and product teams during roadmap gating; decisions are often ad-hoc and lack measurable exit criteria.
- Sales and customer success need a clearer signal of which initiatives materially move revenue/SLA objectives tied to enterprise deals.
- Leadership asked for a lightweight decision runway to speed quarterly resource re-allocations without breaking rollout plans.

Goals (outcome-oriented):
1) Reduce cross-team roadmap re-prioritization time by 30% (measured as median days between a change request and official capacity re-allocation).
2) Ensure every company OKR has a primary and secondary initiative with explicit success metrics and an owner.
3) Provide gating rules so initiatives can be paused or accelerated based on 3 automated signals (usage, latency, eval quality).

Deliverables:
- Outcome Tether ledger (Google Sheet + exportable CSV) with columns: OKR, Owner, Initiative, Start, Planned Completion, Quantitative success metric(s), Current evidence sources (dashboard links), RACI, Decision runway (timebox), Pause/Accelerate gates, Dependencies, Severity if unimplemented.
- A Confluence playbook that documents the decision runway process, stakeholder approvals, and escalation path to execs.
- Two dashboards: a leadership summary (OKR -> initiative health scoreboard) and an operational view for squads (detailed metrics + gating triggers).
- Implementation plan for a quarterly cadence: intake -> assessment -> runway decision -> execute.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every company OKR in the active quarter has at least one linked initiative in the ledger with owner and metric defined.
- At least three teams (Serving Runtime, Console, Dedicated) have seeded their initiatives into the ledger.
- Dashboard surfaces at least one of the three automated signals for every initiative (usage, latency, eval regression).
- Confluence playbook reviewed and approved by PM, Eng, Design, and GTM leads.

Stakeholders and RACI (high level):
- R: PM leads (Ava Chen, Marcus Patel) for ledger maintenance and cadence facilitation.
- A: Head of Product for final runway endorsement.
- C: Engineering leads (Serving runtime, Console, Dedicated), Design lead, Customer Success.
- I: Finance and Sales for downstream forecasting.

Milestones and timeline:
- Week 0 (by 2026-02-28): draft ledger template + Confluence outline. (done)
- Week 1 (by 2026-03-06): seed with 12 initiatives across product/orgs and wireframes for dashboards. (in progress)
- Week 3 (by 2026-03-20): cross-functional review and gating thresholds agreed.
- Week 6 (by 2026-04-15): pilot cadence with two teams and leadership sign-off.

Key trade-offs discussed:
- Level of prescriptiveness: We debated a strict gating policy (hard stop/pause) versus advisory heuristics. Decision: start with advisory gates plus automatic notifications; escalate to hard stops after two quarters of predictable false positives.
- Automation surface area: Building live gates into Redwood Console is ideal, but timeframe pushes this to Q3. Interim: dashboards + weekly cadence calls.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Teams lean on qualitative narratives instead of quant metrics. Mitigation: Require at least one measurable signal per initiative to be allowed on the leadership scoreboard.
- Risk: Dashboard instrumentation gaps. Mitigation: Work with telemetry/infra (ENG-22401) to prioritize missing metrics for the pilot scope.

Artifacts and links:
- Draft ledger (Google Sheet): https://go.redwood.example/sheets/outcome-tether-draft (edit access to PM+Eng leads)
- Confluence playbook: https://confluence.redwood.example/display/PM/Outcome+Tether+Playbook
- Leadership dashboard (Looker): https://looker.redwood.example/dashboards/okr-initiative-scoreboard
- Operational dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.example/d/operational/initiative-health
- Related PRD: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AbCdEfGh/view (PRD: OKR alignment pilot)
- GitHub tracking epic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/roadmap/issues/112

Open decisions and next steps:
- Confirm the three automated signals and thresholds (proposal in sheet, feedback due 2026-03-10).
- Agree the escalation path to execs: suggested threshold is when an initiative misses two sequential monthly signals and impact is "high".
- Identify pilot teams for April runway (suggested: Serving runtime, Dedicated autoscale, Console cost breakdown).

Notes on cross-functional cadence:
- Cadence will be asynchronous-first: ledger updates + evidence posted; weekly 30m triage focused on runway actions with rotating facilitator. Quarterly deep-dive with execs for sign-off.

Implementation tasks (short list):
- PM: finalize ledger columns and seed initiatives (owners: Marcus, Ava).
- Eng: instrument missing metrics and add dashboard panels (ENG-22401).
- Design: create one-pager visuals for leader view and operational view.
- GTM: add revenue-linked initiatives and forecast lines.

Success metrics post-pilot (30/60/90 days):
- 30d: ledger adoption: 3 teams active, 100% OKRs mapped.
- 60d: median decision time reduced by 20%.
- 90d: two runway decisions executed (one paused, one accelerated) with documented impact.

If approved, this will become the canonical company-level approach for aligning cross-functional initiatives to OKRs and will be rolled into the PM handbook and planning templates.
